title: Gleirschklamm Gorge Scharnitz
name: Gleirschklamm Gorge Scharnitz
kurzbeschreibung: The Gleirschklamm in the Naturpark Karwendel near Scharnitz: pristine wilderness, emerald-green whitewater, and narrow wooden walkways along the cliff.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wildly romantic Gleirschklamm is situated in the municipality of Scharnitz in the heart of the Naturpark Karwendel in the Seefeld region at an altitude of around 970 to 1,070 metres. As an untouched side branch of the Hinterautal, the gorge forms the dramatic breach of the roaring Gleirschbach, which has carved deep ravines and crystal-clear rock pools into the limestone massif. Compared to more heavily frequented gorges, the Gleirschklamm has completely preserved its pristine alpine wilderness character and is considered a true insider tip for mountain hikers and peace seekers.

Alpine Elemental Force & Wooden Footbridges

The opening of the gorge looks back on a long tradition of forestry: in bygone centuries, Tyrolean loggers drove massive tree trunks through the narrow ravine down to the Isar river (timber rafting). Today, a narrow, exposed hiking trail leads over historic wooden planks, slender catwalks, and secured wire-rope passages directly above the foaming mountain water. Visitors hike past vertically towering rock flanks beneath which the stream shimmers in mesmerizing shades of turquoise and emerald green. Ferns, mosses, and rare alpine flora line the moist gorge floor. After around 45 minutes of walking, the gorge opens up into the more gently ascending Gleirschtal with sweeping views of the striking peaks of the Gleirsch-Halltal-Kette.

Visit & Getting There

The Gleirschklamm is freely accessible and free of charge during the snow-free summer months from late May to mid-October (winter closure is in effect during the snowy months from November to May). As the wooden footbridges can become slippery when wet, good sure-footedness and a head for heights are essential. Getting there by car: via the B177 (Seefelder Straße) from Seefeld or Mittenwald to Scharnitz; pay parking spaces are available at the Karwendelparkplätze (Länd) at the entrance to the village. By public transport: take the Karwendelbahn train (ÖBB/DB) to Scharnitz station, from where a scenic 40-minute walk via the Isarpromenade and the Hinterautal leads to the entrance of the gorge.

Tips

Traversing the gorge requires ankle-high hiking boots and sure-footedness; the trail is not suitable for young children or anyone suffering from severe vertigo. Combine the hike with a scenic continuation to the rustic Möslalm or Kristallhütte in the Gleirschtal, where homemade alpine cheese and traditional Tyrolean cold-cut platters are served.
